# Time-boxed technical spikes: resolve decisions before building

Curated by Skill Harbor — @github's skill for creating time-boxed technical spike documents that resolve critical decisions before implementation: one question per spike, with a full document template — Summary (spike objective, why it matters, timebox, decision deadline), Research Questions (primary + secondary), Investigation Plan (research tasks with a checklist, success criteria: the spike is complete only when a clear recommendation is documented and a proof of concept completed where applicable), Technical Context (related components, dependencies on other spikes/decisions, constraints), Research Findings (investigation results, prototype/testing notes, external resources), Decision (recommendation, rationale, implementation notes, follow-up actions), and Status History (🔴 Not Started → 🟡 In Progress → 🟢 Complete). File naming `[category]-[short-description]-spike.md` in a spikes directory; categories covered (API integration, architecture & design, performance & scalability, platform & infrastructure, security & compliance, UX); agent best practices (evidence-based decisions, clear recommendations, dependency tracking, outcome-focused — every spike must end in an actionable decision); and a 3-phase research strategy (gather → validate → decide).
